cases.purpose: Lookup USR1 using signal, deliver its number to the verified fixture child with caught disposition, observe handler/wait behavior, and prove a separately ready sibling still responds and exits normally.
cases.oracle: Independent GNU Bash kill -l maps names and numbers; GNU Bash kill/trap/wait exercises the identical owned-child protocol. The child installs its trap using the semantic signal name, independent of the candidate lookup result. Linux SIGUSR2=12 gives default wait status 140; caught traps exit 23. All behavior runs only in the disposable VM.
cases.comparison: Exact readiness, delivery, handler, inherited-ignore and wait-status markers on both implementations. PIDs are compared to their own launched children and never normalized from observed output; unrelated sibling delivery is detected by its response and wait status. Supervising-shell wait diagnostics are retained separately.
cases.candidate_script:
expected=USR1
mode=caught
selector=number
[[ $(type -t signal) == builtin ]] || exit 96
lookup_num() { signal -n "$1"; }
lookup_name() { signal -s "$1"; }
target= sibling=
cleanup() {
  local child children
  children=" $(< /proc/$BASHPID/task/$BASHPID/children) "
  for child in "$target" "$sibling"; do
    [[ $child =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || continue
    if [[ $children == *" $child "* ]]; then
      builtin kill -KILL "$child" 2>/dev/null || :
    fi
    { wait "$child"; } 2>>"$HOME/signal-wait.log" || :
  done
  exec 3>&- 4>&- 5>&- 6>&-
  /usr/bin/rm -f target.in target.out sibling.in sibling.out
}
trap cleanup EXIT
n=$(lookup_num "$expected") || exit 90
canonical=$(lookup_name "$n") || exit 91
independent_n=$(builtin kill -l "$expected") || exit 92
[[ $n =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ && $n -le 64 ]] || exit 93
[[ $n == "$independent_n" ]] && printf 'number=matches-reference\n' || printf 'number=DIFFERS\n'
[[ $canonical == "$expected" ]] && printf 'name=roundtrip\n' || printf 'name=DIFFERS\n'
exec 3<>target.in 4<>target.out 5<>sibling.in 6<>sibling.out
if [[ $mode == ignored ]]; then
  (trap '' "$expected"; exec "$BASH" --noprofile --norc child.sh "$expected" ignored 3<target.in 4>target.out 5>&- 6>&-) &
else
  "$BASH" --noprofile --norc child.sh "$expected" "$mode" 3<target.in 4>target.out 5>&- 6>&- &
fi
target=$!
"$BASH" --noprofile --norc child.sh "$expected" caught 3<sibling.in 4>sibling.out 5>&- 6>&- &
sibling=$!
IFS=' ' read -r -t 4 ready target_reported <&4 || exit 94
[[ $ready == ready && $target_reported == "$target" && $target -gt 1 ]] || exit 95
IFS=' ' read -r -t 4 ready sibling_reported <&6 || exit 94
[[ $ready == ready && $sibling_reported == "$sibling" && $sibling -gt 1 && $sibling != "$target" ]] || exit 95
printf 'owned-child-pids=verified\n'
if [[ $mode == ignored ]]; then
  IFS= read -r -t 4 line <&4 || exit 94
  printf '%s\n' "$line"
fi
if [[ $selector == number ]]; then deliver=$n; else deliver=$canonical; fi
builtin kill -s "$deliver" "$target"
delivered=$?
printf 'delivery=%d\n' "$delivered"
if (( delivered != 0 )); then printf 'quit\n' >&3; fi
if [[ $mode == caught && $delivered == 0 ]]; then
  IFS= read -r -t 4 line <&4 || line=missing-handler
  printf '%s\n' "$line"
elif [[ $mode == ignored ]]; then
  printf 'ping\n' >&3
  IFS= read -r -t 4 line <&4 || line=no-response
  printf 'ignored-after-delivery=%s\n' "$line"
  printf 'quit\n' >&3
fi
{ wait "$target"; } 2>>"$HOME/signal-wait.log"
rc=$?; target=
if [[ $mode == default ]]; then
  printf 'target-wait=%d\n' "$rc"
  [[ $rc -eq $((128 + independent_n)) ]] && printf 'default-status=128+signal\n' || printf 'default-status=DIFFERS\n'
else
  printf 'target-wait=%d\n' "$rc"
fi
printf 'ping\n' >&5
IFS= read -r -t 4 line <&6 || line=no-response
printf 'sibling-after-delivery=%s\n' "$line"
printf 'quit\n' >&5
{ wait "$sibling"; } 2>>"$HOME/signal-wait.log"
rc=$?; sibling=
printf 'sibling-wait=%d\n' "$rc"

[[ $(type -t signal) == builtin ]] || exit 96

target= sibling=

sibling=$!
IFS=' ' read -r -t 4 ready target_reported <&4 || exit 94
[[ $ready == ready && $target_reported == "$target" && $target -gt 1 ]] || exit 95
IFS=' ' read -r -t 4 ready sibling_reported <&6 || exit 94

fi
if [[ $selector == number ]]; then deliver=$n; else deliver=$canonical; fi
builtin kill -s "$deliver" "$target"
delivered=$?
printf 'delivery=%d\n' "$delivered"
if (( delivered != 0 )); then printf 'quit\n' >&3; fi
if [[ $mode == caught && $delivered == 0 ]]; then

rc=$?; target=

  [[ $rc -eq $((128 + independent_n)) ]] && printf 'default-status=128+signal\n' || printf 'default-status=DIFFERS\n'

cases.purpose: Lookup RTMIN+1 using signal, deliver its number to the verified fixture child with caught disposition, observe handler/wait behavior, and prove a separately ready sibling still responds and exits normally.
cases.oracle: Independent GNU Bash kill -l maps names and numbers; GNU Bash kill/trap/wait exercises the identical owned-child protocol. The child installs its trap using the semantic signal name, independent of the candidate lookup result. Linux SIGUSR2=12 gives default wait status 140; caught traps exit 23. All behavior runs only in the disposable VM.
cases.comparison: Exact readiness, delivery, handler, inherited-ignore and wait-status markers on both implementations. PIDs are compared to their own launched children and never normalized from observed output; unrelated sibling delivery is detected by its response and wait status. Supervising-shell wait diagnostics are retained separately.
